**Part 2: Filtering and Inspecting Country-Year Data**

**Estimated time:** 2-3 hours

In this assignment, you will use one cleaned country-year dataset built for the
summer assignments. Each row is one country or economy in one year. Most
indicators come from World Bank World Development Indicators. Governance
indicators come from the Worldwide Governance Indicators. The teaching team uses
a cleaned CSV snapshot so everyone works with the same data and your assignment
can knit reliably.

## Why knit?

Knitting runs this document from top to bottom in a fresh R session. If the knit
works, your code and written answers can be reproduced in order.

## Packages and data

Run this chunk first.

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"))

if (!requireNamespace("tidyverse", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("tidyverse")
}

library(tidyverse)

dev <- read_csv("../data/development_indicators_2026.csv")
dictionary <- read_csv("../data/development_indicators_dictionary_2026.csv")
```

## Inspect before filtering

Always inspect a dataset before filtering it.

```{r}
head(dev)
glimpse(dev)
nrow(dev)
```

The data dictionary explains the variables, sources, and units.


## Values that exist

Before filtering on a text value, check the exact values in the data.

```{r}
dev |> distinct(region)
dev |> distinct(income_group)
```

Now inspect countries inside one region before choosing a country filter.

```{r}
dev |>
  filter(region == "Sub-Saharan Africa") |>
  distinct(country) |>
  arrange(country)
```

## Filtering rows

The `filter()` function keeps rows that satisfy a condition.

```{r}
dev |>
  filter(country == "Ghana")
```

You can filter to a year:

```{r}
dev |>
  filter(year == 2023)
```

You can filter to one region:

```{r}
dev |>
  filter(region == "Sub-Saharan Africa")
```

You can combine filters with `&`, which means "and."

```{r}
dev |>
  filter(region == "Sub-Saharan Africa" & year == 2023)
```

You can filter to low- and middle-income countries using the helper column
`is_lmic`.

```{r}
dev |>
  filter(is_lmic == TRUE & year == 2023)
```

The required exercises use `assignment_sample == TRUE`, which keeps the focus on
countries that are good teaching examples for these assignments.

```{r}
dev |>
  filter(assignment_sample == TRUE & year == 2023)
```

## Sorting with arrange()

Use `arrange()` to sort rows.

```{r}
dev |>
  filter(region == "Sub-Saharan Africa" & year == 2023) |>
  arrange(life_expectancy) |>
  select(country, year, life_expectancy)
```

Use `desc()` to sort from high to low.

```{r}
dev |>
  filter(region == "Sub-Saharan Africa" & year == 2023) |>
  arrange(desc(life_expectancy)) |>
  select(country, year, life_expectancy)
```

## Creating variables with mutate()

Use `mutate()` to create new columns.

```{r}
dev |>
  mutate(gdp_per_capita_thousands = gdp_per_capita_ppp / 1000) |>
  select(country, year, gdp_per_capita_ppp, gdp_per_capita_thousands)
```

You can save the result as a new object.

```{r}
dev_small <- dev |>
  mutate(gdp_per_capita_thousands = gdp_per_capita_ppp / 1000)
```

## Missing values

Some development indicators are missing for many country-years. Poverty and
Gini data often come from household surveys, which are not conducted every year
in every country.

```{r}
dev |>
  filter(country == "Rwanda") |>
  select(country, year, poverty_rate, gini)
```

Use `!is.na()` to keep rows where a value is not missing.

```{r}
dev |>
  filter(country == "Rwanda" & !is.na(poverty_rate)) |>
  select(country, year, poverty_rate)
```
